player_0.content: New plan: I failed because I used the letter "a" multiple times in words like "Layton," "play," "day," "are," "and," "bold," "now," and "good" (wait, "good" is fine, but "Layton" has two 'a's). My strategy of writing a standard poem ignored the strict constraint of using "a" at most once. Next time, I will first list common words that do not contain the letter "a" (e.g., "sky," "blue," "run," "joy," "free," "sun," "wind," "cloud," "bird," "fly," "high," "soft," "drift," "warm," "bright," "be," "go," "now," "life," "is," "good," "you," "up," "look," "by," "here"). I will then construct the song using only these words, ensuring the name "Layton" is either omitted or replaced with a nickname that fits the constraint, or I will use "Layton" exactly once if the prompt implies the name itself is exempt (though safer to avoid it entirely or count its 'a's). I will rigorously check every single word before writing to ensure the total count of "a" does not exceed one.
